record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.context_brief: QCD critical point existence and location
record.original_question: Does the QCD critical point exist in the temperature-density phase diagram of QCD, and if it does, what are its critical temperature and density coordinates? Equivalently, can a first-principles finite-density QCD calculation establish either the existence or the non-existence of a critical endpoint separating crossover and first-order behavior in baryonic matter?

evidence.quote: However, the QCD critical point has not been discovered so far. Although there are many phenomenological studies regarding the QCD critical point, the location of the critical point on the phase diagram is not known. Even the very existence is not established.
The first-principle study based on QCD is needed to establish the existence or non-existence of the QCD critical point, and if it does exist, to determine the critical temperature and density.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the SU(3) gauge theory of quarks and gluons, at nonzero temperature T and nonzero baryon chemical potential μ_B. As a function of (T, μ_B), the theory exhibits a phase structure separating a hadronic phase from a quark–gluon plasma phase. At μ_B = 0, lattice QCD with physical quark masses establishes that the transition is an analytic crossover at a pseudocritical temperature T_pc ≈ 155 MeV. Model studies and effective theories suggest that at sufficiently large μ_B the transition becomes first order, in which case the line of first-order transitions must terminate at a second-order critical endpoint (the "QCD critical point") in the (T, μ_B) plane.

Resolve the following from first principles within full QCD (e.g., via a controlled finite-density lattice calculation that overcomes the fermion sign problem):

(a) Determine whether a critical endpoint exists in the QCD phase diagram in the (T, μ_B) plane, i.e., a point at which a line of first-order chiral/deconfinement transitions terminates in a second-order transition.

(b) If such a critical endpoint exists, determine its location, i.e., the values (T_c, μ_B^c).
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2025–2026, the existence and location of the QCD critical endpoint remain unresolved. Recent continuum-extrapolated lattice QCD work (using entropy-contour extrapolations from imaginary chemical potential) excludes a critical point at μ_B < 450 MeV at the 2σ level but cannot establish its existence; the methodology itself is debated. Experimental searches (RHIC Beam Energy Scan / STAR) continue. No first-principles proof of existence or non-existence has been established.

status_evidence.title: Lattice QCD constraints on the critical point from an improved precision equation of state
status_evidence.snippet: At 2σ the existence of a critical point at μ_B < 450 MeV can be excluded; the location of the critical endpoint cannot be unambiguously bracketed and the analysis does not provide a clear proof of existence.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice study constrains but does not establish existence/location of the QCD critical point.

status_evidence.title: Comment on 'Lattice QCD constraints on the critical point from an improved precision equation of state'
status_evidence.snippet: The entropy-contour method does not provide a direct probe of critical behavior and cannot support model-independent constraints on the location of the QCD critical endpoint.
status_evidence.claim: The lattice methodology used to constrain the critical point is contested.

status_evidence.title: Search for the QCD Critical Point in High Energy Nuclear Collisions: A Status Report
status_evidence.snippet: Status report on ongoing searches for the QCD critical point at RHIC; existence remains under active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental search for the critical point is ongoing and inconclusive.
